Point (geometry).subject: Applied Sciences
Point (geometry).question: The _____ was Fundamental object of geometry.
Point (geometry).fact: In geometry, a point is an abstract idealization of an exact position, without size, in physical space, or its generalization to other kinds of mathematical spaces. As zero-dimensional objects, points are usually taken to be the fundamental indivisible elements comprising the space, of which one-dimensional curves, two-dimensional surfaces, and higher-dimensional objects consist.

Point (geometry).subject: Applied Sciences
Point (geometry).question: In classical _____ geometry, a point is a primitive notion, defined as "that which has no part"
Point (geometry).fact: In classical Euclidean geometry, a point is a primitive notion, defined as "that which has no part".

Point (geometry).subject: Applied Sciences
Point (geometry).question: Many constructs within _____ geometry consist of an infinite collection of points that conform to certain axioms
Point (geometry).fact: In the two-dimensional Euclidean plane, a point is represented by an ordered pair (x, y) of numbers, where the first number conventionally represents the horizontal and is often denoted by x, and the second number conventionally represents the vertical and is often denoted by y. This idea is easily generalised to three-dimensional Euclidean space, where a point is represented by an ordered triplet (x, y, z) with the additional third number representing depth and often denoted by z.

Point (geometry).subject: Applied Sciences
Point (geometry).question: In addition to defining points and constructs related to points, _____ also postulated a key idea about points, that any two points can be connected by a straight line
Point (geometry).fact: In addition to defining points and constructs related to points, Euclid also postulated a key idea about points, that any two points can be connected by a straight line. This is easily confirmed under modern extensions of Euclidean geometry, and had lasting consequences at its introduction, allowing the construction of almost all the geometric concepts known at the time.

Point (geometry).subject: Applied Sciences
Point (geometry).question: This is easily confirmed under modern extensions of _____ geometry, and had lasting consequences at its introduction, allowing the construction of almost all the geometric concepts known at the time

Point (geometry).subject: Applied Sciences
Point (geometry).question: {\displaystyle \operatorname {dim} _{\operatorname {H} }(X):=\inf\{d\geq 0:C_{H}^{d}(X)=0\}.} A point has _____ dimension 0 because it can be covered by a single ball of arbitrarily small radius
Point (geometry).fact: If S ⊂ X and d ∈ [0, ∞), the d-dimensional Hausdorff content of S is the infimum of the set of numbers δ ≥ 0 such that there is some (indexed) collection of balls { B ( x i , r i ) : i ∈ I } {\displaystyle \{B(x_{i},r_{i}):i\in I\}} covering S with ri > 0 for each i ∈ I that satisfies ∑ i ∈ I r i d < δ. {\displaystyle \sum _{i\in I}r_{i}^{d}<\delta .} The Hausdorff dimension of X is defined by dim H ⁡ ( X ) := inf { d ≥ 0 : C H d ( X ) = 0 }.
